title: Reduce queue resonance through model-aware scaling and tenant pacing
creator: Sofia Kim
description: Summary: After the 2025-02-12 hosted GPU exhaustion incident we observed recurring ‘queue resonance’ — rapid buildup/decay cycles in tenant queues caused by correlated long-sequence bursts and conservative autoscaler hysteresis. Root causes: (1) autoscaler thresholds tuned for average token rates, not sequence-length skew; (2) single global admission policy that treats all models/tenants identically; (3) KV-cache coldness causing long tail inference times under burst; (4) lack of tenant-level token pacing to limit tail amplification. This ticket tracks the design, implementation, test, and rollout of mitigations that reduce queue amplification and avoid repeated capacity drain events.
action_items: Design and implement model-aware scaling heuristics: autoscaler reads per-model avg_seq_len and token-rate to compute required GPU slot count. Owner: Kunal. ETA: 2025-03-08.
Add tenant pacing layer: implement per-tenant sliding token-window (tokens/minute) with gradual backpressure (soft 429s then hard 503) and telemetry. Owner: Priya Singh. ETA: 2025-03-01.
KV-cache warming daemon: lightweight prefetcher that enqueues predicted KV prefixes for hot tenants/models to reduce cold-run latency. Owner: Ricardo Alvarez. ETA: 2025-03-10.
Autoscaler hysteresis tuning and fast-up path: shorten scale-up decision window for long-sequence models; extend scale-down delay when queues are unstable. Owner: SRE team. ETA: 2025-03-05.

Introduce fast-degrade fallback policy: when pool saturation crosses emergency threshold, route >95th-percentile length requests to quantized/shorter-context model variant. Owner: ML Infra. ETA: 2025-03-07.
Add new telemetry: per-pool avg_seq_len, inflight_tokens_by_tenant, kv_cache_hit_rate, queue_resonance_index (custom metric). Owner: Observability. ETA: 2025-02-28.
Chaos and load simulation: create synthetic tenant workloads that reproduce resonance and validate mitigations before rollout. Owner: Load Engineering. ETA: 2025-03-03.
Canary rollout and monitoring: 10% tenant canary, monitor queue-90p, tail latency, and 5xx rate for 48h before wider rollout. Owner: Kunal + Oncall. ETA: 2025-03-12.
Post-release retrospective and KPI review: measure percent reduction in queue-length variance and incident recurrence. Owner: PM (Ava Rodriguez). ETA: 2025-03-25.
acceptance_criteria: Canary (10% tenants) shows >=40% reduction in queue-length variance and >=30% reduction in 95p latency during synthetic long-seq bursts.
No increase in steady-state error rate or cost >5% for the canary group.
Telemetry for new metrics is available in Grafana and alerted on (SLOs configured).
Runbook updated with new mitigation knobs and oncall playbook entries.
All code changes have 2 reviewers, CI green, and security self-review completed.
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket opened after initial postmortem; triage meeting with SRE/ML Infra/Autoscale team. Assigned to Kunal.

2025-02-20: Data analysis completed — confirmed high correlation between 95p sequence length spikes and queue resonance. Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-991999-queue-resonance-analysis.
2025-02-24: Prototype model-aware scaling algorithm implemented (simulation harness). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4287 — awaiting review.
2025-02-26: Tenant pacing prototype integrated into admission controller; added feature flag 'tenant_pacing_v1' and local test harness. Initial lab tests show reduced amplification in synthetic runs.
2025-02-28: Observability added new metrics (kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_seq_len) to staging Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-hosted/capacity-staging?panelId=7.
2025-03-01: Load team ran chaotic long-seq burst scenarios — resonance reproduced. Begin full integration tests for KV warmer and canary policy.
2025-03-03: PRs merged for tenant pacing and telemetry. Canary config prepared (10% tenants picked by hashed tenant id range).
2025-03-04: Canary rollout started to staging group; monitoring alarms set (queue_resonance_index > 0.3 triggers paging). Early signals look promising — queue variance down ~45% in canary cohort.
Next: complete KV-warmer tests, finalize autoscaler hysteresis tuning, then promote canary to 50% if stable for 48h.
notes: Tradeoffs: tenant pacing may add additional 429s for high-volume customers during bursts. Decision: prefer soft 429 with advisory header + automatic retry guidance before hard reject.
Cost considerations: KV warming introduces small extra GPU cycles; estimate <3% steady-state overhead for hot pools. This is acceptable vs repeated incidents cost.
Fallback behavior: fallback to quantized model variant needs explicit per-model quality budget; PM to own customer communication for affected models.
Owner escalation: If canary shows adverse impact >10% error increase, abort rollout and revert feature flags immediately.
